title: IA-MNS Identity
heading: Principal administrator, bootstrap and recovery
text:
Principal administrator, bootstrap and recovery
`pnpm identity:bootstrap` (server shell, runtime configuration) prints a single-use 30-minute URL `/identidade/inicial#<secret>` when no active owner exists; `--break-glass` issues one even if owners exist. Both are audited. The page creates the owner with a local account and then requires TOTP before administration.
Administration (`/admin`, `/identity/admin/*`) requires the owner role, a TOTP-assured session (unless a non-production policy makes the second factor optional), and recent authentication for changes (policy window, default 30 minutes). The last active owner cannot be removed or disabled, and owners cannot disable their own TOTP.
Owners create Persons with any combination of: a 72-hour single-use local enrollment invitation (`/identidade/convite#enrollment=<secret>`); a Sankhya user selected from the ERP directory; and link invitations for PDT Connect or Sankhya. Associations always point to a real account: Sankhya users are re-read from the directory on the server (missing or expired-access accounts and accounts already linked elsewhere are refused before anything is created), and PDT accounts require the person's proof because PDT exposes no user directory to IA-MNS. The same actions exist for existing Persons, together with a new enrollment invitation and the reset invitation, which removes the local credential and revokes sessions. Invitation secrets travel in URL fragments, which are not sent to servers, and are removed from history on load.
Owners consolidate two Persons of the same individual (`POST /identity/admin/persons/{personId}/merge`) when they cannot be proven together; owners are never the absorbed Person and overlapping providers are refused.
The Sankhya directory (`GET /identity/admin/sankhya-users`) reads the DBA-provided view named in `SANKHYA_DIRECTORY_VIEW` (columns `CODUSU`, `NOMEUSU`, `NOMEUSUCPLT`, `EMAIL`, `DTLIMACESSO`) in a read-only transaction with its own two-connection pool and a 10-second call timeout, returning at most 20 users. It is off while the view is not configured ([PH-08](../project/human-actions.md#ph-08)). It needs only `SANKHYA_IDENTITY_ISSUER`, not the Om session connector, so it is not gated by PH-11.

title: IA-MNS Identity
heading: WhatsApp numbers
text:
WhatsApp numbers
Owners link at most one WhatsApp number to a Person in **Administração → Pessoas → WhatsApp** (`PUT`/`DELETE /identity/admin/persons/{personId}/whatsapp`), with the same owner, second-factor and recent-confirmation checks as the rest of administration ([ADR-0036](../adr/0036-add-whatsapp-as-an-agent-channel-authorized-by-owner-linked-numbers.md)). Nobody can link, change or remove their own number in any other way, and there is no self-service through WhatsApp; **Minha conta** only shows the number.
**Entry.** International form with country code (`+55 11 98765-4321` or `0055…`); spaces, dots, dashes and parentheses are ignored. National numbers are refused (`IDENTITY_WHATSAPP_NUMBER_INVALID`), and a Brazilian mobile without its ninth digit is refused with its own message (`IDENTITY_WHATSAPP_NINTH_DIGIT_REQUIRED`). The number is stored as E.164 digits in `identity_whatsapp_links`.
**Uniqueness.** A number belongs to at most one Person, and so does its deterministic legacy Brazilian form, which WhatsApp may report for older mobile accounts ([identifiers](whatsapp-channel.md#identifiers)); a conflict is `IDENTITY_WHATSAPP_NUMBER_IN_USE`. Only active Persons receive a number.
**Audit.** `whatsapp.linked`, `whatsapp.changed` and `whatsapp.removed` record the owner, the affected Person, the time and only the last four digits, in the same transaction as the change; `whatsapp.confirmed` records the first accepted message.
**Generation.** The Person retains the last allocated WhatsApp link version even after removal. Creation, number changes and transfers allocate a later version under the Person lock in the same transaction as the audit. Recreating a number never reauthorizes work queued for a former link.
**Revocation.** Removing or changing the number, disabling the Person or consolidating it takes effect for the next message and for every reply not yet handed to Meta, because the channel asks identity again before processing and before sending. A changed number forgets what was learned about the previous one.
**Authorization.** For each signature-verified message, identity returns exactly one active Person and that Person's effective permissions computed now, as for a new access token; the number grants nothing by itself. Merging moves the absorbed Person's number to the surviving one when it has none; otherwise the absorbed number is removed.
A linked phone works as a credential without a second factor; see the channel's [residual risks](whatsapp-channel.md#security-notes-and-residual-risks).

**Duration and inactivity.** A direct session ends at sign-in + duration, whatever the use, or when no activity is reported for the inactivity period. The browser reports activity (clicks, typing, scrolling, returning to the tab) with each renewal of its 10-minute access token; renewals of an untouched tab keep the token fresh but do not postpone inactivity. Renewals are serialized across tabs, a tab that returns from sleep renews at once, and a renewal presenting the credential replaced in the last 30 seconds is a concurrent renewal that receives a token without a new credential; later reuse revokes the session. When a session ends, the person returns to `/entrar` with "Sua sessão terminou".
**Recent authentication.** Changes to one's own password, links or second factor need a sign-in or confirmation within the account window; administrative changes within the administrative window. Confirmation uses the password and code, a provider proof, or a new embedded handshake.
**Second factor.** It applies to sign-in with an IA-MNS password (PDT Connect and Sankhya sign-ins are protected by those systems). With `everyone` every such account, and with `administrators` every owner, must use it: an account without it gets `mfa_enrollment_required` after the password (also right after setting a password from an enrollment or reset invitation) and sets up the authenticator before any session opens (`POST /identity/login/mfa-enrollment` and `/confirm`), and cannot remove the factor while required. The code is asked at every sign-in, unless the person chose to remember the browser (offered only when `rememberDeviceDays` > 0, never inside a host page, and to owners only while the requirement is `none`, which production never allows). A remembered browser keeps an HttpOnly `ia-mns-device` cookie whose token is stored hashed in `identity_trusted_devices`; it skips the code but yields an ordinary (not second-factor) session. Password changes, removing the factor, an owner reset or **Voltar a pedir o código em todos** in Minha conta forget remembered browsers.
**Changes.** Saving requires an owner session with the second factor (per policy) and recent administrative confirmation; values outside the limits are refused (`IDENTITY_POLICY_INVALID`), `none` in production is refused (`IDENTITY_POLICY_NOT_ALLOWED`), and newly reduced settings require `acknowledgeReducedSecurity` (`IDENTITY_POLICY_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`). Each change is audited (`policy.updated`) with previous and new values and listed on the screen. Open direct sessions are re-derived at once from their sign-in and last activity (shorter values may end them, including the editor's); second-factor rules apply at the next sign-in, while administration always checks the current rule. Other API instances follow within 15 seconds.
**Not configurable.** Production always requires the second factor for administrators; outside a non-production `none` policy, owners never skip the code through a remembered browser; access tokens stay 10 minutes; embedded sessions renew silently every 10 minutes; ticket, flow and invitation lifetimes, lockout, refresh rotation with reuse detection, rate limits and audit are fixed.

title: IA-MNS Identity
heading: Operational parameters
text:
Operational parameters
Owners administer the [operational parameters](../architecture/configuration.md#operational-parameters) at `/admin` → **Parâmetros** (`GET /identity/admin/parameters`, `PUT /identity/admin/parameters/{key}`, [ADR-0028](../adr/0028-administer-operational-parameters-separately-from-secrets-and-bootstrap-configuration.md)): the AI model, the AI trace level and the WhatsApp channel switch. Identity hosts this administration because it owns the principal administrator; the parameters themselves are declared by the runtime catalog and read by their owning consumers. Default provider groups have separate identity-owned storage and endpoints (`GET /identity/admin/provider-groups`, `PUT /identity/admin/provider-groups/{provider}`), despite appearing on the same page.
**Who.** The same check as all administration: the owner role, a second-factor session (per the authentication policy), and recent administrative confirmation for changes. Anyone else receives `IDENTITY_ACCESS_DENIED` for listing, reading and changing; hiding the tab is not the protection.
**What is shown.** Each parameter's value in use, the installation default, whether an owner value or the default applies, who changed it and when, when a change takes effect, and the last 20 changes. Environment variable names, secrets and bootstrap settings are never part of the response, and unknown keys (including secret names) are `IDENTITY_PARAMETER_NOT_FOUND`.
**Changes.** A change applies only to the version the owner read (`IDENTITY_PARAMETER_CONFLICT` otherwise); values outside the parameter's domain are `IDENTITY_PARAMETER_INVALID`, values this environment refuses (content tracing in production) are `IDENTITY_PARAMETER_NOT_ALLOWED`, and `null` restores the installation default. Each change is audited as `parameter.updated` with the parameter, previous and new effective values (lists comma-separated), whether it was a reset and the new version, in the same database transaction as the change, so a change never persists without its audit event; parameters never hold secrets. The installation default `OPENAI_MODEL` must satisfy the same identifier domain as `ai.model`, so the default is always a value an owner could also save.
**Effect.** No restart: the AI model applies to the next AI request, the trace level to the next turn, and the WhatsApp switch to the next message. Default group selection applies on the next verified provider sign-in, without a restart.

title: IA-MNS Identity
heading: Security properties
text:
Security properties
Secrets (tickets, refresh credentials, recovery codes, assertion ids) are 256-bit random values or high-entropy codes stored only as SHA-256. Passwords are scrypt verifiers; TOTP secrets are AES-256-GCM sealed. None are logged or returned after creation.
Failures for unknown logins and wrong passwords are identical, and a dummy hash equalizes timing. Lockout is temporary (from the 5th failure: 1, 2, 4… up to 60 minutes). Login, verification and flow endpoints are rate limited.
Cookie-authenticated endpoints (refresh, provisioning and consolidation by cookie, signed-in detection at login start) accept only same-origin web requests (`x-ia-mns-client: web`, `Sec-Fetch-Site`, `Origin`). A consolidation ticket is bound to the session that proved both profiles.
Audit (`identity_audit_events`) is append-only for the runtime role and stores only allowlisted codes.
All identity responses are `Cache-Control: no-store`.

title: IA-MNS Identity
heading: Deployment requirements
text:
Deployment requirements
HTTPS `IA_MNS_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`; the signing and encryption keys in the secret store, generated for each environment with `pnpm identity:keys --output <new file>` (or `node dist/cli/identity-keys.js` beside a build), which writes an owner-only file and prints no key material. Never reuse local keys.
Serve the web and the API under the same origin: the API process serves the web build (`ORION_WEB_ROOT`) and answers under `/api`, the browser path of `PDT_IDENTITY_REDIRECT_URI` (`https://<ia-mns>/api/identity/pdt/callback`) and of the Sankhya callback (`https://<ia-mns>/api/identity/sankhya/callback`) ([ADR-0029](../adr/0029-serve-the-web-and-api-from-one-origin-behind-restricted-trusted-proxies.md)).
Every response sends `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, which keeps the real `Origin` on the web's `fetch()` writes (a native form POST would carry `Origin: null` and fail the cookie endpoints' check), and `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'` except `/embed/pdt` and `/embed/sankhya`, which allow only `PDT_EMBED_ORIGIN` and `SANKHYA_EMBED_ORIGIN` respectively; the serving API derives this from the identity configuration. The development and preview servers reuse the provider origins from the root ignored `.env.local`, with shell values taking precedence. An explicit `ORION_WEB_EMBED_ANCESTORS` overrides both surfaces; an empty value disables framing.
Behind the TLS reverse proxy, `ORION_TRUSTED_PROXIES` lists only that proxy, so login and verification limits apply per client; issuer, redirects and cookie security still come from `IA_MNS_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`, never from forwarded headers.
The first owner comes from `pnpm identity:bootstrap`, or `node dist/cli/identity-bootstrap.js` beside a build, run once with the runtime configuration.
Configuration names are listed in the [generated configuration reference](../generated/configuration/api.md).

title: IA-MNS Identity
heading: Limits and next steps
text:
Limits and next steps
The embedded Sankhya integration passed in the Sankhya development Om only; the direct-URL Sankhya sign-in page is pending ([PJ-25](../project/implementation-plan.md#current-work)), and production needs PH-11, PH-14 and PH-17. The embedded PDT integration passed with a local PDT Connect ([PJ-27](../project/implementation-plan.md#current-work)); HTTPS homologation and production are PH-12. Development, synthetic and proof-of-concept results are not production evidence.
Passkeys, e-mail recovery, SCIM or automated deprovisioning from Sankhya/PDT, Sankhya-group-to-permission mappings, explicit denials and restrictions of product lookup are not implemented. Deactivating a user in Sankhya or PDT stops new proofs; existing IA-MNS sessions end at their expiry or on owner action.
PDT authorization data (permissions and stores) is not yet mapped to IA-MNS capabilities; future PDT capabilities must re-authorize with PDT at execution time, as the contract requires.
Retention of identity data, audit and sessions follows the shared-deployment policy still pending in [PH-09](../project/human-actions.md#ph-09).

title: IA-MNS Identity
heading: Replacing the former provider permission policy
text:
Replacing the former provider permission policy
Migration `202610210001_identity_provider_groups` starts both provider selections empty. Before shared use, create or choose the desired groups, review their permissions and restrictions, then select them in Parâmetros ([PH-13](../project/human-actions.md#ph-13)). Existing explicit grants and memberships remain. The former `access.providerGrants` parameter and `IA_MNS_PROVIDER_GRANTS` environment variable no longer grant access; historical rows and audit remain for evidence. A broader group grant is united with personal grants, so a restricted personal grant cannot narrow an unrestricted default group.

title: Product Lookup
heading: Scope
text:
Scope
Product lookup is one corporate-agent capability that answers, in Portuguese, which products of the selected registration match conditions. This page owns the VR Master semantics: "Quais produtos são banana fruta?", "Quais produtos são do centro de custo SECOS?", buyers, combinations, exclusions, synonyms and refinements. [Sankhya product lookup](sankhya-product-lookup.md) owns its separate dictionary-discovered dimensions and runtime credential requirements. It lists products with the interpretation that selected them; it never calculates sales, prices, stock or margins, which remain the [sales capability](sales-chat.md). It needs `products:read`. title: Product Lookup
heading: UI acceptance
text:
UI acceptance
VR Master is ready for first user acceptance with the configured restricted reader. Sankhya Runtime access is now [verified](../project/runtime-access-verification.md) with `IA_MNS_RO`; PH-08 retains business confirmations. Automated authenticated journeys use synthetic identities/data; no authenticated browser journey against these real ERPs has been executed by the agent. A configuration check proves neither database availability nor user acceptance.
Use Node 24.13.0 and pnpm 11.25.0. From the repository root run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. Start the existing IA-MNS PostgreSQL; for the already provisioned repository Compose database use `docker compose --env-file infra/local/.env -f infra/local/compose.yaml start`. Use `pnpm db:local` only for the local database setup described in [setup](../setup.md#corporate-agent-and-local-postgresql), since it also configures application database URLs. Keep the existing ignored `.env.local`, OpenAI key, identity keys and restricted `VRMASTER_DB_*` settings. Do not bootstrap a replacement owner or change an existing account.
Use `IA_MNS_LOCAL_ACCESS=false` and ordinary IA-MNS sign-in. Start `pnpm -C apps/api dev` with the existing `IA_MNS_RO` and `ia_mns` Runtime settings. Both sources now have [verified reader access](../project/runtime-access-verification.md). Normal loading excludes administrative keys and never loads either Discovery file. Never use administrative credentials to work around a Runtime error. Restart an already running API to ingest the new directory setting.
In a second terminal run `pnpm -C apps/web dev`. Open `http://127.0.0.1:5173` (the configured `IA_MNS_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`; use the same origin as existing sign-in), and sign in with the existing authorized account and its second factor if required. Do not enter database or OpenAI credentials in the browser.
An existing principal administrator already has every product permission. For another authorized tester, a principal administrator opens the account menu → **Administração** → selects the existing person → **Permissões**, clicks **Conceder** on **VRM-PRD-01 Consultar produtos** under Pilar da Terra (VR Master) (`products_vrmaster:read`; SNK-PRD-01 for Sankhya) and confirms it reads **Efetiva por concessão individual**. Review default provider groups separately in Parâmetros; their members inherit any product permission an owner grants to those groups. The tester signs out and in to obtain an updated access token. No new database migration or new owner is required for this permission.
Open a new conversation, choose **Pilar da Terra (VR Master)** in **Fonte** above the composer, and send the cases below one at a time. Start a new conversation for independent cases; keep a conversation for refinements and numbered choices. Check the displayed source, interpretation, criteria, total and product list. Counts describe the live catalog and may change.
Message / action
Expected acceptance behavior
`Quais produtos são banana fruta?`
Fresh-banana classification, descendants included, chips and raw materials excluded; five products in the 2026-10-11 reference
`Quais produtos do centro de custo SECOS?`
Indirect product → section → cost center; 19,091 products in the reference, bounded visible list with total
`Quais produtos de mercearia não são doces?`
Hierarchical inclusion plus exclusions; interpretation explains nodes chosen and preserves sweet corn
`Quais produtos de hortifrúti são pesáveis?`

`Quais produtos são banana?` then a displayed option number
Explicit ambiguity where applicable; the number chooses the offered interpretation, preserving the source
`Quais produtos da compradora Ana?` (fictional example), then choose a real offered buyer if unmatched; `Desses, quais são do centro de custo SECOS?`
Grounded current buyer, safe unknown-name clarification, then combined filtering; no fabricated personal value
`Quais produtos estão ativos?`
Explicit unavailable-dimension explanation until PH-27 and catalog validation; no invented status
Change to `Tudo` with both catalogs configured
Asks which ERP, without combining or translating identifiers
Change to **MNS (Sankhya)** with the verified Runtime reader and ask `Quais produtos possuem unidade alternativa KG?`
Separate Sankhya state, indirect registration relation, unique products; 3,035 in the reference
For Sankhya also reproduce literal BATATA description (382), base KG (794), active revenda plus BATATA (97), and a literal EPI certificate from an authorized known record; see [its validated scope](sankhya-product-lookup.md#filtering-capabilities). Unsupported buyer/classification semantics must remain explicit. No real Sankhya UI success is claimed before account provisioning and this journey.
Product model requests now have a bounded **30-second per-request budget**, with zero automatic runtime retries; sales and routing retain their **20-second** default. The agent cancels the entire asynchronous turn after **90 seconds**, propagates the same abort signal, and checks cancellation before saving successful state. ERP queries have separate bounded deadlines. UI polling does not extend these budgets; closing the page is not a cancellation operation. Tests cover provider timeout, caller cancellation, Oracle interruption and safe cleanup. The second acceptance-preparation VR run included a completed 17.8-second model call and one transient provider retry (only the opt-in runner retries); that tail latency justifies modest product-specific headroom. The provider retry was not classified as a timeout and is not proof of one. Both live product runners share the runtime's 30-second constant, replacing Sankhya's former offline 40-second override. Failures retain a safe reference; verify the conversation outcome before resubmitting.

text:
VR Master product schema
Discovered on 2026-10-11 through read-only transactions with bounded queries: PostgreSQL catalogs (columns, primary, unique and foreign keys, indexes, privileges), aggregate checks of the data and comparison with the [sales reference SQL](sales-chat.md#vrmaster-sales-semantics) and PDT Connect queries. The runtime account (PH-19) reads only nine tables but all catalog metadata; data checks of the other tables used temporary discovery credentials the owner supplied for this investigation only, inside read-only transactions. title: Product Lookup
heading: Observations that shape answers
text:
Observations that shape answers
The mercadológico has 21 level-1, 208 level-2, 1,622 level-3, 5,200 level-4 and 8,914 level-5 nodes. Deeper levels frequently hold brands and package sizes, sometimes producer names.
Cost center SECOS is assigned to 13 sections, including two named INATIVO and FEIRA INATIVO; four sections have no cost center. A level-2 cost center and its level-3 child often share a name; a name therefore resolves to the subtree.
Nodes named `MP …` or `MATERIA PRIMA` hold production inputs of bakery, butchery and rotisserie (fresh bananas used as ingredients, for example).
Nodes named INATIVO group retired registrations by convention, but about a third of their products are still active in a store, while many products elsewhere are active in none. Only per-store registration states activity.
The classification can be wrong for individual products: the live regression found a product of another brand filed under a brand node.
Indexes support the executed shapes: subtree membership and section lookups take milliseconds; the combined cost center and buyer case took 26 ms in `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`; candidate retrieval for a classification takes about one second.

title: Product Lookup
heading: Interpretation
text:
Interpretation
**Categories.** The person's concept ("banana") and its qualifier ("fruta") are kept apart. The model chooses among real nodes found by name, their children and nodes whose product descriptions mention the words. With "fruta", "in natura" or "fresca" it keeps the product itself and leaves out flavored, processed and prepared products. Raw-material and inactive-classification nodes are included only when asked. Without a qualifier, when the word covers clearly different kinds, the person chooses between numbered interpretations, typically the product itself or every product mentioning the word.
**Cost centers** follow the section of each product, including sub-centers; the answer says so.
**Buyers** are the registered buyer of each product. Names are matched by the application from the person's words (whole words); several matches, or none, become numbered options.
**Combinations.** Different dimensions combine with AND. Two values of one single-valued dimension ("do comprador A ou do B", "banana e maçã") are a union; overlapping classifications ("mercearia" and "doces") intersect. Exclusions remove subtrees or records; including and excluding the same thing is asked about.
**Answers** state every criterion with its resolved records or classification paths, exclusions and business rule, counts per section, notes (inactive products not yet distinguishable; products under inactive classifications; raw materials included) and up to 200 products in alphabetical order with the exact total.

text:
Required scenarios and results
Live runs on 2026-10-11 used the real VR Master through the restricted account and the configured model (`gpt-6.1-sol`). "Equal" means the resolver's complete selection equals the set of an independent hand-written SQL query; no record values are recorded here.
Scenario
Result

The five fresh bananas under FLV › FRUTAS › BANANA, without its chips node; snacks, yogurts, sweets, a sunscreen brand and the two raw-material bananas excluded. Equal. This classification is the regression reference for "banana fruta"; no earlier classification existed in the repository.

19,091 products of the 13 sections linked to SECOS (sub-center included). Equal.
C — products of a buyer named in the question
The first name matched exactly one active buyer. Equal.

487 products. Equal.
E — hierarchies, synonyms, attributes, exclusions
Mercearia without sweets (sweet corn kept), hortifrúti (FLV) that are pesáveis, raw-material bananas only (2), a brand within a category, two buyers as a union, refinement of a buyer, two buyers with similar first names kept apart, a literal description, cost center with category exclusions, an ambiguous word answered with an option number (no second model call), a contradiction, an unknown name with options, and unavailable or out-of-scope requests: all as expected.
The final acceptance-preparation [live regression](../architecture/semantic-product-resolution.md#maintaining-the-catalog) passed 24 of 24 turns with the shared 30-second product request budget and zero provider retries. The catalog check reported no difference from the live schema, grants or invariants. The restricted VR reader has no superuser, database/role creation, replication or row-security bypass privileges, owns no public tables, and has no writable public tables; its default transactions are read-only with a 30-second statement timeout. These are dated observations of the configured account, not a replacement for catalog verification after grants change.

title: Product Lookup
heading: Privacy and data flow
text:
Privacy and data flow
Product descriptions, classifications, buyers and results are CONFIDENTIAL; buyer names are personal data. The model receives the person's messages, application replies, dimension meanings and, to choose classifications, classification paths, counts and up to three example product descriptions per candidate; never buyer names, prices, costs, stock, sales, table names or credentials. Requests use `store:false`, which does not establish zero provider retention. Options holding personal data appear only in the structured result. Traces follow the [AI tracing levels](../architecture/ai-interpretation.md#ai-tracing-and-observability). No product data is committed: the regression dataset with real codes stays in the ignored local folder.

title: Product Lookup
heading: Limits and open questions
text:
Limits and open questions
Lists include inactive products until per-store status is readable ([PH-27](../project/human-actions.md#ph-27)); the answer says so.
Whether sections named INATIVO count under SECOS, what "fabricante" should mean, the operational meaning of "pesável" and whether provider links should grant product permissions (SNK-PRD-01, VRM-PRD-01) automatically are owner decisions ([PH-28](../project/human-actions.md#ph-28)).
Model judgment can differ between runs for borderline products and is shown in the answer; transient provider errors fail the turn (observed in a few percent of calls during the 2026-10-11 runs); a classification criterion makes two model calls.
Product lookup can feed [semantic sales selections](sales-chat.md#semantic-product-selections) with both permissions. An explicit "desses produtos" reuses the same ERP's completed selection; qualified concepts can also be resolved directly inside sales. Current registration membership does not reconstruct historical classification/responsibility.

title: Product Lookup
heading: Verification
text:
Verification
Unit, synthetic-PostgreSQL, evaluation and browser checks are listed in [semantic product resolution](../architecture/semantic-product-resolution.md#verification). On 2026-10-11 the earlier live curated evaluation passed 49 of 49 cases (72 turns). Acceptance preparation then passed all six product-routing cases/seven turns with zero retries, including the verified FLV synonym and both ERP routes.
The complete `pnpm validate` passed in the actual working tree on 2026-10-11: 383 API tests, 63 web unit tests, 12 browser component tests, 35 end-to-end journeys, builds, bundle checks, internal-HTTPS smoke and all static/reference checks. Installed Git OpenSSL was added only to that validation process PATH. All 83 focused resolver tests passed, including real module composition over disposable PostgreSQL with authenticated HTTP, permission denial before ERP access, both adapters, source-scoped persistence and idempotent replay. The browser suite uses synthetic identities and ERP data. It exposed a real permission UI bug: the controlled checkbox's value was read after asynchronous execution; capturing it before execution fixed grant/revoke persistence, with all ten identity journeys passing across Vite and built serving. No real user's grants were changed.
Documentation discovery now follows the portal's Git scope: tracked and non-ignored new Markdown, with no symlink/junction redirects. Two source-validator tests cover private-note exclusion, tracked files even when newly ignored, new public documents, tracked deletions and redirected directories. The original 128 pending implementation files remain present; ignored private notes and `.env.local` were not edited. The existing application database was started without replacing its users or settings. The local API and web return success, and anonymous conversation access remains 401. This verifies availability and authentication boundaries, not real authenticated UI acceptance. No ERP database was modified, no remote CI or deployment was run, and PH-08/PH-29 remain open.

text:
Sales Capability
[Corporate agent](corporate-agent.md) · [Project plan](../project/implementation-plan.md) · [Setup](../setup.md) · [Architecture decision](../adr/0018-bound-natural-language-sales-to-a-read-only-query-capability.md) · [Sources decision](../adr/0027-select-the-sales-source-in-the-interface-and-read-each-source-separately.md) · [AI interpretation](../architecture/ai-interpretation.md)

title: Sales Capability
heading: Scope and acceptance
text:
Scope and acceptance
The first business capability of the IA-MNS corporate agent lets an authorized sales reader ask questions in Portuguese about the sales of MNS (Sankhya) and Pilar da Terra (VRMaster), receive real aggregates, and continue with related questions. The person chooses the source in the interface ([sources](#sources)). Example: “Quanto vendi de maçã por mês nos últimos 3 meses?” followed by “E comparado ao mesmo período do ano passado?”. Generic monetary questions use the source's monetary measure: VLRLIQUIDO in Sankhya, `valortotal` in VRMaster. Ordinary literal-description filters remain supported; [semantic product selections](#semantic-product-selections) add verified registration conditions without changing sales measures.
Acceptance requires an executable API/web workflow, validated interpretation, deterministic calculations, explicit missing configuration and provider errors, contextual comparisons, useful suggestions, no arbitrary SQL, and no ERP writes. Actual ERP reconciliation and live model interpretation additionally require the credentials tracked in the [human checklist](../project/human-actions.md#ph-08) ([PH-20](../project/human-actions.md#ph-20) for VRMaster). Synthetic tests do not establish the business accuracy of a real database.
Only net value, quantity, weight (Sankhya only), totals, monthly breakdown, product breakdown, and comparisons with the prior year or immediately preceding equal-length period are supported. Other processes, returns as a separate report, customer/seller/store transaction filters, margins, costs, taxes, automation, exports, login, and deployment are outside this capability. Current product cost centers, buyers and other enabled registration conditions come from the separate [product resolver](product-lookup.md), then restrict eligible sales. They are not sale-time buyer or transactional cost-center filters. Durable conversation history belongs to the agent module. A capability user reads every source and all companies represented by each reference; `sales:read` grants both sources and no tenant or per-company isolation is implied.

title: Sales Capability
heading: Semantic product selections
text:
Semantic product selections
The normal conversational sales path can now use the same verified resolver as product lookup. A user must hold the sales permission and the product permission of the selected source (for example VRM-VEN-01 and VRM-PRD-01); without the product permission the answer names the missing code. Select one ERP in **Fonte**. Qualified product concepts and catalog conditions are resolved before sales, using the existing grounding, relationships, hierarchy expansion and ambiguity choices. Simple literal phrases retain their existing behavior; explicit description requests stay literal. Unavailable conditions do not become description guesses or overall totals. Unsupported sales/customer/seller/store/price/stock requests remain unsupported as a whole.
Conversational scenario
Expected behavior
VR Master: `Quanto vendi de banana fruta no mês passado?`
Resolves the fresh-banana classification and exclusions, then calculates sales for the complete selection with the reference grain
VR Master: `Quanto vendi dos produtos do centro de custo SECOS em setembro de 2026?`
Product → current section → cost center membership restricts sales; no assumption of a cost center on sale rows
First `Quais produtos são banana fruta?`, complete any displayed choice, then `Quanto vendi desses produtos no mês passado?`
Explicitly reuses that source's completed selection; a lookup in another ERP or an unanswered choice asks for identification/confirmation
`Quanto vendi de banana fruta?`, then supply only the requested period
Retains the original semantic request, with no ERP sales query until the period and selection are complete
An ambiguous sales request, then a displayed numbered product option
The choice resumes sales with its saved period; no sales query precedes the choice
`E comparado ao mesmo período do ano passado?`, `E a quantidade vendida?`, or `Detalhe por produto`
Retains the same semantic scope; only the stated analytical fields change
`E de todos os produtos?`, or an unrelated new overall-sales request
Clears the semantic scope; a new request never silently inherits the last lookup
Sankhya: `Qual o valor vendido dos produtos com unidade alternativa KG em setembro de 2026?`
Uses verified indirect unit membership; duplicate alternate-unit rows do not duplicate sales
Select `Tudo` for a semantic request
Asks for one ERP; ordinary literal/all-product sales still query both separately
The answer shows the applied semantic criteria and source. Selection uses the **current product registration**, including its current buyer/category, equally for the requested and comparison periods. It does not reconstruct historical assignments or switch the existing measure to another business calculation. Registration members with no eligible reference sales contribute zero; product counts and counts of sold products are different concepts. Breakdown and quantity-unit rules remain unchanged, including no VR Master weight measure.
The backend compiles complete key membership, never the first 200 displayed products. Semantic sales lists at most 100 sold products per period and warns when the list is incomplete; totals still cover all members. The 500-row aggregate cap still refuses an oversized detailed query rather than returning partial figures. Metadata/catalog/access validation and cancellation fail closed. A catalog-version change asks for identification again. No new ERP grants or writes are needed for already enabled dimensions.
[`products-sales.test.ts`](../../apps/api/test/products-sales.test.ts) covers orchestration/permission/source/version/pending-request boundaries; the real-composition HTTP test covers both permissions and adapters; disposable PostgreSQL tests compare actual sales with independent selection SQL and protect totals above display bounds; the Oracle driver boundary checks binds and both comparison periods. Browser coverage renders provenance and follows lookup → numbered choice → sales with intercepted synthetic responses. `pnpm -C apps/api products:sales:regression --model` runs Runtime-only independent aggregate reconciliation and normal model interpretation; it does not authenticate through a browser. Live and complete-gate evidence is recorded in PJ-37. Full VR Master business reconciliation in PJ-29 and PH-08 unit/currency confirmations remain separate.
On 2026-10-12, Runtime-only live reconciliation passed **eight checks**: four independent aggregate comparisons (VR literal description and indirect cost center, Sankhya base and alternate units), two model-driven semantic sales requests, and two explicit same-ERP lookup-reuse requests. All compare current and previous-year periods using the existing reference grain, with no runtime retries. Deterministic scenarios including reference reads/metadata took approximately 1.5–8.9 seconds; model scenarios took approximately 4.9–14.8 seconds. These are local end-to-end observations, not production benchmarks or complete business reconciliation. The first description fixture used a non-normalized phrase and was corrected to match the resolver's normalized AST; final checks all passed.
Final `pnpm validate` passed in the actual working tree: **432 API tests, 63 web unit tests, 13 browser component tests and 35 end-to-end journeys**, plus builds, bundle checks, internal-HTTPS smoke and all static/generated-reference checks. Installed Git OpenSSL was added only to the validation process PATH. The 19 integration scenarios include permission revocation for retained execution, protected semantic history/replay, exact source isolation, pending choices/periods, literal compatibility, stale catalogs and cancellation. The unavailable-VR-weight regression ensures no registration/sales queries run until a supported measure is requested. Disposable PostgreSQL proves full totals for 205 sold products while listing only 100, and current buyer responsibility across both periods. All 172 files pending before this task remain present. No ERP writes, grants, credentials/account changes, remote CI or deployment were performed. No authenticated real-ERP browser journey is claimed.

title: Sales Capability
heading: Sources
text:
Sources
The agent interface offers a selector beside the message box with exactly `MNS (Sankhya)`, `Pilar da Terra (VR Master)` and `Tudo`; it starts at `MNS (Sankhya)`. The web keeps the choice in memory while the application is open, across conversations, and sends it with each turn as `source` (`sankhya`, `vrmaster` or `all`); a reload starts again from `MNS (Sankhya)` and nothing is stored as a preference. The API records the source with the turn ([agent](corporate-agent.md#persistent-conversations-and-context)). The selection replaces the conversational "Sankhya or VRMaster?" question decided on 2026-10-06, which was never implemented ([ADR-0027](../adr/0027-select-the-sales-source-in-the-interface-and-read-each-source-separately.md)).
**The selection decides, never the text.** `MNS (Sankhya)` queries only Sankhya and `Pilar da Terra (VR Master)` only VRMaster. Source and company names in a message neither switch, add nor filter a source: the interpreter ignores them, the application drops a source name placed in a filter, and a message naming another source receives an application-authored notice that the selected source was used.
**`Tudo` queries both, separately for ordinary sales.** The same literal/all-product analysis plan runs in both sources in parallel. The answer has one section per source with its provenance, status and own totals, and says that values are not summed. A semantic product scope asks for one ERP. No combined figure exists without a later product decision.
**Failures stay attributed.** With `Tudo`, a source that is unavailable, not configured or too broad is reported in its section beside the other source's result, and the failure is logged with the turn; the turn fails only when both fail. With a single source, its failure fails the turn and leaves the conversation state unchanged.
**Measures per source.** Net value and quantity exist in both sources; weight only in Sankhya. A weight question with VRMaster alone is answered as unavailable without querying it; with `Tudo`, the VRMaster section says the measure is unavailable.
**Literal plans remain source-independent.** Changing the selector and asking a follow-up (for example "E em agosto?") reuses the ordinary active analysis in the newly selected source. Semantic plans keep their source-scoped selection; a selection from another ERP is never translated or silently removed.
The application layer runs the adapters through the source-neutral `SalesReader` port ([reader.ts](../../apps/api/src/features/sales/reader.ts)). The Oracle adapter knows only the Sankhya reference and the PostgreSQL adapter only the VRMaster reference; they share the port, the scope check of aggregate rows and the literal product-phrase matching ([product-match.ts](../../apps/api/src/features/sales/product-match.ts)), not SQL or connections.

title: Sales Capability
heading: Sankhya sales semantics
text:
Sankhya sales semantics
The canonical executable reference is [query.ts](../../apps/api/src/features/sales/query.ts), transcribed from the owner's SQL on 2026-10-01. Preserve its complete DISTINCT projection, required inner joins, optional joins, adjusted-price precedence, and exclusions. In particular:
Confirmed notes require `CAB.STATUSNOTA = 'L'`, product usage `M` or `R`, excluded operation codes `1002, 915, 9599, 905, 575, 930, 568, 515, 450, 460, 1006, 1008`, and excluded group `85007003`.
The final reference restricts computed `TIPMOV = 'V'`. The computed movement maps bonus sales to `B`, so bonus sales and returns are excluded. Do not subtract returns from the final totals merely because signed return measures exist inside the CTE.
VLRLIQUIDO uses nonzero `AJI.AD_VLRTOTFIN`, then nonzero `ITE.AD_TOTALAJUSTADO`, then `ITE.VLRTOT - ITE.VLRDESC`, subtracts `ITE.AD_VLRTOTALBONIFI`, and applies the reference movement sign.
Quantity uses QTDNEG and is grouped separately by CODVOL; different units never share a total. Monetary values assume BRL, which must be confirmed by the owner. Weight uses QTDNEG × PESOLIQ. The ERP weight unit has not been verified; the UI does not label it kilograms. Missing or nonpositive PESOLIQ produces a warning without changing the reference calculation.
Dates use DTNEG. The inclusive user end date becomes an exclusive next-day boundary so timestamps throughout that day are included. The supplied BETWEEN query needs its end bind to include that same day for reconciliation.
Product matching is a literal, case/accent-insensitive phrase bounded by non-alphanumeric characters, with whitespace normalized. Regex metacharacters are escaped before binding. A product word cannot match the prefix of an unrelated product word. The answer lists products with sales in either requested period, not all catalog products without sales. Generic all-product queries omit the match list.
Join fan-out and duplicate collapse follow the owner's reference. This may retain duplicate effects from multiple adjustment/origin/lot matches; removing or choosing an adjustment requires reconciliation and a separate rule. Product predicates run before DISTINCT, and the lot subquery considers only controls belonging to eligible items; all lot matches for those controls remain eligible. This prunes irrelevant work without choosing a lot or adjustment or changing the projected grain. No schema, index, grant, migration, or object is created in Sankhya.

title: Sales Capability
heading: VRMaster sales semantics
text:
VRMaster sales semantics
The canonical executable reference is [vrmaster-query.ts](../../apps/api/src/features/sales/vrmaster-query.ts), transcribed on 2026-10-07 from the owner's reference SQL ([PH-18](../project/human-actions.md#ph-18)), a PDT Connect dashboard query over `venda`.
Sales are the rows of `public.venda` that survive the reference's joins: inner joins to `produto`, `loja`, the store's `fornecedor`, `produtoaliquota` for the product in the store's state, `aliquota`, and the product's level-1 `mercadologico`; left joins to `centrocusto` and `comprador`. Every join is preserved as supplied, including its cardinality, because dropping one could change which sales count. Only the columns IA-MNS reports are projected; the reference's cost, tax, margin and profit computations are not used.
Every store counts. The reference's `venda.id_loja = ANY(:lojas)` parameter is omitted: its inner join to `loja` already admits exactly the sales of existing stores, so omitting the parameter equals passing every store.
Dates use `venda.data`; the inclusive end date becomes an exclusive next-day boundary, as in the reference.
Net value is the sum of `venda.valortotal` and is labeled "valor total". Quantity is the sum of `venda.quantidade` per `produto.id_tipoembalagem`, labeled by the packaging-type identifier because the packaging-type table is outside the reference and the account's grants; different types are never added. VRMaster has no reviewed weight.
Product matching applies the shared literal phrase to `produto.descricaocompleta`: accented letters are translated before `upper()` so the match does not depend on the database's character classification, whitespace is collapsed, and the pattern is a bound value with its metacharacters escaped.
Table names are schema-qualified (`public.`), so a role `search_path` cannot redirect them. Product labels are `id - descricaocompleta`.
Whether the reference's `calculos` step filters rows could not be read from the supplied excerpt; the transcription assumes it only derives columns. The [reconciliation](../project/human-actions.md#ph-20) compares IA-MNS with the full reference and must confirm or correct this.

title: Sales Capability
heading: Interpretation and computation
text:
Interpretation and computation
The server uses the OpenAI Node SDK Responses API, through the structured-model port, with one forced strict `interpret_sales_message` function call. The interpretation reports a decision (analyze, clarify for genuine ambiguity, or reject unsupported scope), how the message relates to the conversation, and only what the message states; the application merges it into the structured conversation state, asks for missing information, and compiles a bounded query ([AI interpretation](../architecture/ai-interpretation.md)). All public messages, including clarification and rejection, are application-authored; model text never becomes a public sales answer. The model cannot supply arbitrary clarification text or monetary claims. Requests that require unsupported scope are rejected rather than partially answered. The model receives the current Sao Paulo date, recent sales exchanges with the application's replies, and the structured state (last executed filters and any unanswered request). Missing periods require clarification; a later reply that supplies only the period completes the request it answers. The model names the period form and the application computes its dates; periods that have not started are asked again and periods over 366 days explain the limit. “Last N months” defaults to the last N completed calendar months; including the current month must be explicit. This month/year ends today; last N days includes today and N-1 preceding dates. Weight requests, including kg, select weight rather than quantity grouped by KG; no unverified weight conversion is implied. Follow-ups, including identifying considered products, preserve prior filters unless explicitly changed. The interpretation never chooses the source: since interpreter `sales-interpreter/2026-10-07.1`, names of the sources, companies or systems (MNS, Sankhya, Pilar da Terra, VR Master) are neither filters nor unsupported, while a store filter remains unsupported.
All tool output is checked at the provider boundary and then validated by the application. Both current and derived comparison date ranges are real calendar dates from 2000 onward, at most 366 inclusive days, and never future dates. Descriptions have 2–80 characters. Each period, including monthly zero filling, is limited to 500 aggregate rows and 100 matched products; the combined comparison list has at most 200 unique products. Excessive results fail visibly without returning incomplete totals. Empty aggregates retain no synthetic zero row. There is no SQL tool, generated SQL, agent delegation, or vector database.
Current and comparison queries of one source share one read-only transaction and snapshot: Oracle `SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY`, PostgreSQL `BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY`, always rolled back. Decimal strings are converted to 50-digit decimal arithmetic for totals and percentage changes. Monthly results fill missing months with zero for known units. A zero comparison base has an undefined percentage, not infinity. Prior-year leap days clamp to February 28. The previous-period comparison uses an equal number of days, rather than assuming whole months. Replies, tables, and suggestions are built from validated results; sales numbers are not authored by the model.

title: Sales Capability
heading: Access and restrictions
text:
Access and restrictions
Each source has its own permission ([ADR-0037](../adr/0037-grant-identified-per-source-permissions-to-people-and-groups-with-data-restrictions.md), [identity](identity.md#authorization)): **SNK-VEN-01** (`sales_sankhya:read`) for MNS (Sankhya) and **VRM-VEN-01** (`sales_vrmaster:read`) for Pilar da Terra (VR Master). A selected source the person may not read is never queried. With **Tudo**, it appears as a denied section beside the readable source, naming its permission code; when no selected source may be read, the answer lists the missing codes before any interpretation or ERP read.
A grant may be restricted. The sales module enforces each dimension inside the reviewed reference query, as a bound predicate on the same aliases in both selections of the Sankhya reference (eligible lot controls and sale rows) and in the VR Master base selection. Filtering admits rows; it does not change joins, cardinality or the DISTINCT projection, so admitted rows count exactly as in the unrestricted reference.

title: Sales Capability
heading: Identity, privacy, and context
text:
Identity, privacy, and context
Sales execution requires the source's sales permission, with its current data restriction computed by identity ([access and restrictions](#access-and-restrictions)), under Orion's verified bearer principal, or explicit local access. The [agent](corporate-agent.md#persistent-conversations-and-context) owns durable conversation identity, concurrency, context and history. Sales context stores structured conversation state (last executed plan and query, unanswered request, bounded exchanges with application-authored replies); ERP result rows are not model context. The context does not depend on the source. The legacy `/sales/chat` endpoint always uses Sankhya. Failed turns preserve prior filters. The legacy sales endpoints keep their original 30-minute/12-question in-memory semantics for compatibility, while the product exclusively uses durable agent endpoints.
The explicit `IA_MNS_LOCAL_ACCESS=true` mode is for a single developer on loopback only. Configuration rejects it in production or on a public listener; requests also require a loopback client/host, a local browser origin, and the custom client header, and reject cross-site fetches. It grants the local developer the sales-read capability. Do not expose the development Vite proxy or tunnel it; local mode is not a shared environment authentication system. Production requires configured providers and a trusted verifier at startup. A concrete issuer/login remains conditional under PJ-05.
Sales, questions, filters, and product descriptions are CONFIDENTIAL. Credentials are RESTRICTED. The browser holds token/context/results in memory and clears them on credential changes; only the light/dark theme preference uses browser storage. Protected responses use no-store. New conversation preserves history; explicit deletion removes persisted conversation/context/turns. Model requests use `store:false`, which does not establish zero provider retention or account-specific policy. Only questions and filter context go to OpenAI, never sales rows, prices, customer names, credentials, or raw schema. Users must avoid putting unrelated confidential information or credentials in questions.
Provider exceptions produce safe public error envelopes plus one correlated, allowlisted diagnostic, including the provider/stage and bounded public Oracle/OpenAI error codes. Provider/stage remain internal and never include raw messages or configuration. Rollback/close failures remain provider failures and prevent returning an unverified success. No prompt, result, query binds, Oracle connect descriptor, VRMaster host or account, or secret enters logs. Chat input is limited to 2,000 characters and 12 KB transport size; actor rate limit is 15 questions per minute. Model timeout is 20 seconds, Oracle round-trip timeout 45 seconds, pool wait 5 seconds, and execution deadline 90 seconds. VRMaster statements stop after 30 seconds (the account's own limit, repeated in the transaction), locks after 5 seconds, the client gives up after 35 seconds, connections after 5 seconds, and an aborted turn ends its connection. With `Tudo`, both sources run in parallel within the same deadline. Agent acceptance returns immediately and its browser polls actual progress. The legacy sales route overrides the foundation socket inactivity timeout to 95 seconds, while other routes retain their existing budget. Real ERP queries exceeded the original 10-second round-trip limit, so the bounded budgets now accommodate the measured workload. Limits are process-local, not a distributed quota.

title: Sales Capability
heading: Local execution and external verification
text:
Local execution and external verification
Follow [setup](../setup.md#sales-chat) and the generated [configuration reference](../generated/configuration/api.md). Oracle node-oracledb 7 supports Oracle 12.1 in Thin mode; if an actual authentication/network feature requires Thick mode, configure a compatible Oracle Client directory. Client 19 or 21 supports this database version; newer clients are not automatically compatible with older servers ([driver compatibility matrix](https://node-oracledb.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user_guide/installation.html)). The account must have CREATE SESSION and SELECT only on the reference tables, with schema resolution supplied by the DBA. No login/provider or real ERP account is provisioned by this repository.
The 2026-10-01 read-only audit connected to Oracle 12.1.0.2 with Client 19.32 after the configured Client 11.2 failed with DPI-1050 and Thin mode failed with NJS-116. Nine structured-query scenarios matched the supplied SQL's aggregates in a shared read-only snapshot: monthly net value, month to date, rolling 30-day weight, quantity by unit, product breakdown, previous year, equal-length prior period, accent/case equivalence, and no matching sales. The complete 46-column reference projection also matched for the current three-month product scope. Returns and bonus movements were present in the source and excluded by the final sales filter. Actual HTTP injection with the real Oracle adapter passed annual comparison and empty-result handling using a controlled planner; this is not a live natural-language test.
The audit exposed unrelated description-prefix matches, a comparison product list exceeding the original cap, and Oracle work exceeding the original timeout. Word boundaries now exclude unrelated prefixes, both periods contribute to the product list, limits reject truncation, and eligible-control pruning reduces work while retaining the reference projection. Oracle response shape/numeric checks reject malformed results rather than inventing empty sales. Small fetch batches in this legacy Oracle/Thick stack produced an intermittent difference in one complete record, although database-side MINUS in both directions returned no differences and aggregates matched. Fetching the complete bounded result together matched every field; the adapter now aligns its fetch array size with each result cap. This workaround does not establish the precise driver/server cause, which remains a DBA investigation under PH-08.
No business totals, credentials, or connection descriptor are committed as evidence. The owner later configured a key manually and explicitly authorized reuse. Ten actual language requests, eight original-SQL reconciliations, and a real-browser sales query passed; see [live verification](../project/live-sales-verification.md). Synthetic tests remain distinct evidence. The supplied account also has broad write privileges, which the DBA must remove by providing a dedicated reader. Weight-unit and currency confirmation remain owner actions.
Boundary tests use the real OpenAI SDK with synthetic HTTP responses and Oracle connection doubles. API injection tests exercise actual Fastify authorization, context, validation, and error envelopes. Browser journeys exercise the generated SDK with intercepted synthetic sales responses, while the unavailable-configuration path reaches the real emitted API. These checks do not replace validation against Oracle 12.1 or a live model. Run the full [validation gate](../validation.md) before handoff. On the real ERP, compare at least an adjusted item, a bonus exclusion, a return exclusion, multiple adjustment joins, accented descriptions, mixed units, missing weight, month end, and both comparison periods against the reference. No verification operation writes ERP data.

title: Sales Capability
heading: VRMaster
text:
VRMaster
Set the `VRMASTER_DB_*` settings of the [setup](../setup.md#sales-chat) with the dedicated read-only account of [PH-19](../project/human-actions.md#ph-19) (`CONNECT`, `USAGE` on `public`, `SELECT` only on the nine reference tables, `default_transaction_read_only = on`, 30-second statement timeout); never the PDT Connect account. On 2026-10-07 the VRMaster server answered the PostgreSQL TLS request negatively, so its connection needs `VRMASTER_DB_SSL_MODE=disable`, which sends the credentials and sales data unencrypted on that network; the default `verify-full` refuses to connect without TLS. Without VRMaster settings, selecting it reports the source as not configured.
The adapter's tests run the fixed SQL on PostgreSQL 16 with a synthetic VRMaster schema and the PH-19 grants: period totals and inclusive dates, monthly and product grouping, accent- and case-insensitive whole-word product phrases, comparisons, packaging-type quantities, every reference join (excluded and included rows), bound text that looks like SQL or a regular expression, no transaction left open, cancellation of a blocked read and unavailable or refused connections. They establish the transcription's behavior, not agreement with the real VRMaster; that is the reconciliation of [PH-20](../project/human-actions.md#ph-20), with the queries in [VRMaster reconciliation](../project/vrmaster-reconciliation.md).

title: Sankhya Product Lookup
heading: Availability and scope
text:
Availability and scope
The adapter identifies physical `TGFPRO` registrations through the existing `products` capability and the SNK-PRD-01 permission (`products_sankhya:read`). Choose **MNS (Sankhya)** in the source selector. When both adapters are configured, **Tudo** asks for one ERP: product codes, selections and pending choices remain independent. It does not calculate sales, quantities, conversion factors, prices, stock, legal certificate validity or availability by company.
The configured privileged account is authorized for local discovery only. The runtime refuses ERP object owners and accounts with privileges beyond CREATE SESSION and object SELECT, before executing product queries. The subsequent [owner-authorized provisioning](../project/runtime-access-verification.md) granted the existing `IA_MNS_RO` account its minimum access and verified Runtime execution; PH-08 retains business confirmations. No ERP grants, writes, migrations or procedures were executed. The later [ERP access decision](../security/erp-database-access.md) separates administrative Discovery credential delivery from runtime; actual Runtime grant verification is recorded separately.

title: Sankhya Product Lookup
heading: Dictionary and physical discovery
text:
Dictionary and physical discovery
The [official Data Dictionary documentation](https://developer.sankhya.com.br/docs/dicion%C3%A1rio-de-dados) describes the entity mappings, relationship expressions, calculated fields and properties that must accompany physical metadata. Read-only Oracle discovery on 2026-10-11 reconciled:
Structure
Captured knowledge
`TDDTAB`
Physical table names and business descriptions
`TDDCAM`
Field names, descriptions, calculated/custom flags and expression fingerprints
`TDDINS`
Instance ids/names, inheritance, active state, expression fingerprints and key-script presence
`TDDLIG`
Origin/target instances, direction, mandatory flag, relationship/instance-rule fingerprints
`TDDLGC`
Every mapped field pair, including composite keys
`TDDOPC`
Stored values and descriptive labels, joined through field ids
`TDDPCO`
Additional property names and value fingerprints, including possible interceptors/security rules
Oracle native catalogs
Actual column types/nullability, PK/unique/FK column positions and enabled/validated status, indexes and local synonym resolution
`TGFPRO` has 444 physical columns, 412 dictionary fields and ten custom dictionary fields. Four dictionary fields are calculated (including `TIPO`); none are used by runtime projections. Product-table metadata describes 22 instances and 160 outgoing instance relationships, 63 of which carry relationship/target expressions, conditions or key scripts requiring separate review. The bounded product frontier covers 11 tables, 928 physical columns and 267 outgoing dictionary relationships. The snapshot preserves edges beyond the frontier as discovered candidates; it does not expose them as executable joins. Related tables are `TGFGRU`, `TGFMAR`, `TGFVOL`, `TGFVOA`, `TGFPAP`, `TGFPAR`, `TGFCLP`, `TGFCLA`, `TSICUS` and custom `AD_LISTADCEMB`. The frontier was selected from actual product mappings and relevant two-hop paths; synchronization does not crawl the entire ERP or automatically expand this reviewed scope.
Dictionary expressions, BeanShell, UI reference parameters and key scripts are never executed. Raw expressions/property values are fingerprinted rather than included in the tracked snapshot or model prompt. Metadata contains no ERP product/partner rows, credentials, connection descriptors or database-owner names.

title: Sankhya Product Lookup
heading: Physical registration and JAPE instances
text:
Physical registration and JAPE instances
`Produto` is instance 27, with a dynamic `TSIPAR`-dependent `SERVFILUSOPROD` expression governing service usage `S` and excluding usage `3`; `Servico` is a separate instance (29). Product instance descendants inherit additional rules. These are entity semantics, not unconditional SQL relationships. The adapter explicitly queries physical `TGFPRO`, including services/tariffs, and explains that scope in every answer. It does not claim parity with JAPE `Produto`.
`USOPROD` has 15 descriptive options in `TDDOPC`. Actual registrations also contain `S` (107 rows) and `3` (seven rows), without descriptive options there. Those codes remain included in an unrestricted physical registration query, but are not invented as named domain filters. Complete dictionary option labels take precedence over qualified partial matches; multiple remaining matches require clarification.

heading: Verified relationship graph
text:
Verified relationship graph
Every executable edge records source/destination, all join pairs, conditions, cardinality, meaning, dated evidence, dictionary instance ids, physical constraint and confidence in the catalog. The following edges have high confidence for physical joins; dictionary/JAPE rules are assessed separately.
Path from product

Verified evidence and interpretation

`TGFPRO.CODGRUPOPROD → TGFGRU.CODGRUPOPROD`, many-to-one
Every one of 10,959 products has a valid group; FK and instance mapping agree
Group ancestors
`TGFGRU.CODGRUPAI → CODGRUPOPROD`
672 nodes, maximum depth three; explicit parent ids, including negative root sentinel and special group zero; no numeric prefix assumption
Registered brand

All non-null values reference unique brands; 100 assigned brand ids, distinct from 114 free-text `MARCA` values

18,185 rows cover 4,909 products; composite registration PK `(CODPROD,CODVOL,CONTROLE)`

`CODPROD → TGFPAP.CODPROD`, then `CODPARC → TGFPAR.CODPARC`

The product-to-alternate-unit and product-to-partner-link mappings carry the reviewed `@ref-param[include-in-deep-copy=true]` annotation. Only its exact known fingerprint is accepted as a harmless copy annotation. Arbitrary relationship expressions cannot enter compilation. The preferred-supplier instance instead carries a supplier expression; it is not silently promoted to a general join.
The group parent graph is validated for duplicate keys, cycles, missing positive parents and depth above eight. Oracle traverses explicit parents with `CONNECT BY NOCYCLE`, also bounded to eight. Source nodes carry their actual ancestor ids so the shared resolver can compare containment without ERP-specific arithmetic. Composite bridge registrations retain every mapped join pair; named-value lookup currently requires a single key.

Names alone are insufficient evidence. No relationship was invented to satisfy these questions.

title: Sankhya Product Lookup
heading: Execution and native API evaluation
text:
Execution and native API evaluation
The Oracle adapter owns a pool of at most two connections (queue four, acquisition timeout five seconds), `SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY`, rollback and cancellation, a 15-second per-call timeout and a 30-second operation budget. Results/metadata have explicit row bounds, product lists stop at 200, group nodes at 2,000 and candidates at 60. Identifiers come from the reviewed catalog; all user values are binds. SQL is compiled from the validated AST and never provided by the model. Runtime verification checks used physical/dictionary definitions, keys, mapped relationships, properties, domain options and readable projections before first use and every ten minutes.
[CRUDServiceProvider.loadRecords](https://developer.sankhya.com.br/reference/get_loadrecords) supports root entities, entity paths, parameterized criteria, pagination and calculated-field selection. It could preserve native instance rules and calculated values better than direct physical SQL. However, `ignoreCalculatedFields` defaults to false, `modifiedSince` depends on change logging, and file-based pagination uses server storage. Entity reads may involve application hooks, rules and authorization different from SQL. A documented read endpoint alone does not establish strict absence of side effects in this installation.
Direct read-only SQL is implemented for these verified physical filters and consistent count/list snapshots; nested existence predicates avoid collection expansion. Native API execution is deferred until a separately authorized least-privilege API identity and read-side behavior can be validated. No database credentials were transmitted to the API and no API call was made. Future calculated/JAPE-dependent capabilities should compare authorized API results with known entity behavior rather than translate raw dictionary expressions into SQL.
